newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to pay debts to gold industry in Feb - agency.
newsitem.headline: Russia to pay debts to gold industry in Feb - agency.

text.p: Russia plans to settle debts to the Russian gold industry this month, but intends to finance no more than 30 percent of 1997 production, Itar-Tass news agency quoted Deputy Prime Minister Valery Serov as saying on Friday.
He said the government intended to settle debts left over from 1996 by February.
But he added that the rest of this year's production would have to be financed through other sources.
Serov was quoted as telling a meeting of the commission looking into problems in the north of Russia that the Russian government wanted to help set up a domestic gold market.
Tass also quoted Valentin Tsvetkov, head of the administration of the gold-producing region of Magadansk, as saying the region was actively preparing for free market conditions.

Tsvetkov said the government would still have the first right to gold purchases. If it could not buy all the gold, domestic and foreign firms should be able to step in, although Russian companies would have priority, he said.
In December, a Russian Industry Ministry report said 1996 gold production was likely to fall to around 110 tonnes against 122 tonnes in 1995. It could fall sharply again in 1997, officials have said.
Producers have blamed the expected drop in 1997 output on the absence of a viable precious metals market and exchange.
They have also said that about five percent of all mined gold leaks to the black market, where some producers prefer to get cash at once instead of waiting for months for the government to pay.
